Vide this common judgment, I shall decide the instant three claim petitions filed separately under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, by the claimants seeking compensation on account of fatal ____________________________________________________________ injuries caused to three persons, namely Ravi Kumar, Satish Kumar and Rohit in the same motor vehicular accident, which occurred on 02.02.2018 at around 10:35 p.m., near Petrol Pump,100 Feet Road (Road leading to Durgapuri from Nand Nagri), Nand Nagri, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS Anand Vihar, Delhi.
Three separate DARs were also filed which have been tagged with the respective claim petitions.

2. Brief facts of the case as per claim petitions are that on the aforesaid date and time, all the three deceased persons namely Ravi Kumar, Satish Kumar and Rohit were travelling on a motorcycle bearing no. DL5S-AX-6183 being driven by Rohit and when they reached at the aforesaid place, a truck bearing registration number HR69A-0881 (hereinafter, 'vehicle no.0881' or 'offending vehicle') being driven by respondent no.1 at a very high speed came from Gagan Cinema side and while overtaking the said motorcycle took a sudden left turn without giving any indication and in the process, its rear left side hit the said motorcycle.
As a result of the accident, all the three occupants of the motorcycle fell down on road along with the motorcycle and sustained fatal injuries.
3. In connection with the accident, FIR no.153/2018, under sections 279/337/304-A IPC, was registered at PS Nand Nagri, Delhi on 03.02.2018.

As per FIR, at the spot of accident, motorcycle of victims, bearing registration number DL5SAX-6183 in accidental condition was found lying and three injured persons were already removed to GTB Hospital, where injured Satish vide MLC no.
____________________________________________________________ B-290/3/18 and injured Ravi vide MLC no. B-291/3/18
were declared brought dead, whereas, injured Rohit vide MLC no. A-529/04/18 was declared unfit and during the course of treatment, he died on 03.02.2018.

As per investigation of the case FIR, at the time of the accident, the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1 Vijay Pal, owned by respondent no.2 Parmod and and insured with respondent no.3/ Royal Sundaram General Insurance Company Ltd.

15.

In the present cases, the fatal accident occurred on 02.02.2018 at about 10:35 p.m., near Petrol Pump, 100 Feet Road, Nand Nagri, on road towards Gagan to Durga Puri, Delhi and there were two witnesses who had seen the accident, namely Satish Kumar who has been examined as R3W2 and Rajendra Kumar who has been examined as PW4 as well as CW2 (Court Witness).
Both the witnesses i.e., Satish Kumar and Rajendra Kumar did not after the accident immediately inform the police regarding the accident.

16. After about five days of the accident, on 07.02.2018, Satish Kumar informed the Investigating Officer (R3W1) that the offending vehicle was a truck bearing registration number HR55G-7002 (hereinafter, 'vehicle no.7002').

However, vide complaint/ letter dated 21.02.2018 addressed to DCP, North-East, Satish Kumar informed that he committed mistake in giving the registration number of the offending vehicle reason being that there were two vehicles present at the scene of the accident and the person who had noted down the registration number of the offending vehicle, had mistakenly noted down the registration number of vehicle no.7002, whereas the registration number of the vehicle that caused the accident was HR69A-0881.
17.

The Investigating Officer on the basis of the statements of the above said two witnesses concluded that the accident in question was committed by the vehicle no.0881 without investigating a n y t h i n g a b o u t t h e v e h i c l e n o . 7 0 0 2 a n d f i l e d t h e c h a r g e - s h e e t a g a i n s t t h e ____________________________________________________________ driver of the vehicle no.0881 i.e., the respondent no.1 Vijay Pal.
18.

The interesting part of the case is that the owners of both the vehicles i.e. vehicle no.7002 as well as vehicle no.0881 was the same person, i.e. respondent no.2 Pramod (examined as R3W4 as well as CW1) and the vehicle no.7002 as on the date of the accident was not insured.

Because of this coincidence that the owner of the both the vehicles was one and the same person and the vehicle that was earlier stated to have been the vehicle with which the accident was caused on 02.02.2018 was not insured and the subsequent vehicle that was stated to be the vehicle with which the accident was caused was insured, the respondent no.3/ insurance company has taken the defense in their written-statement that the vehicle no.0881 was not involved in the accident and has been falsely implanted as the vehicle with which the fatal accident was caused.
Because of the specific defense taken by the respondent no.3/ insurer, a specific issue i.e., issue no.2 has been framed.

On 07.02.2018, Satish Kumar met the Investigating Officer at MACT Cell in the Police Station and informed that the accident which had happened on 02.02.2018 at about 10:30 P.M. in which three injured persons were involved had happened with the truck bearing registration number HR55G-7002.

As per the Indian Evidence Act/ Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, a fact (rashness and/ or negligence is not a fact but is an opinion that could be formed on the basis of facts) is said to be proved when after considering the matters before the Tribunal, the Tribunal either believes it to exist or considers its existence so probable that a prudent man ought, under the circumstances of the particular case to act upon the supposition that it exists.
The Tribunal is aware that the strict technical rules of Evidence Act/ Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam are not applicable in the enquiry proceedings,
which are to be conducted under Chapter 12 of Motor Vehicles Act, but the definitions of conclusive proof, may presume, shall presume, proved, disproved etc. are so basic and germane in the enquiry proceedings, which are to be conducted by the Tribunal that these definitions could hardly be said to be the technical rules, rather these definitions are the fulcrum on which the enquiry proceedings are to be conducted by the Tribunal after all before the award could be passed the petitioners have to prove its case on the balance of probability.

However, in the judgment of the Single Bench of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Harsh Mishra; 2016 ACJ 2669, it has been held that mere registration of criminal case/ filing of the charge-sheet is not enough to prove negligence on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and that every fact must be proved either by direct or indirect evidence.
Even, in a case where the driver of the offending vehicle is acquitted by the Criminal Court, the Tribunal on the basis of such fact cannot dismiss the claim petition holding that the driver of the offending vehicle was not rash and negligent in driving the offending vehicle but in the light of the evidence that may be led, the Tribunal has to come to its own conclusion regarding the rashness and negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
77. The Criminal Court can return the finding of guilty only when the prosecution is able to prove the charges beyond reasonable doubt.
In the charges with reference to any offence under Indian Penal Code/ Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, requiring rash and/ or negligence as one of the ingredients of the offence with respect to use of motor vehicle, if the Criminal Court has held guilty, then the verdict of guilty could be taken at the discretion of the Tribunal as sufficient proof before the Claims Tribunal in an enquiry regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
_ to a finding on the touchstone of preponderance of probability/ balance of proof regarding the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the driver, the same has to be culled out/ discerned from the evidence of the witnesses examined before the Claims Tribunal and the contents of the charge-sheet filed by the police which is one of the relevant pieces of evidence.
78. If a holistic view of the evidence as lead by the petitioners/ respondents are taken into consideration by the Tribunal, the rashness and negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle/
respondent no.1 has not been proved by the petitioners.
Rather, it appears that on the balance of probability, neither of the two vehicles i.e. vehicle no.7002 or vehicle no.0881 was involved in the accident that occurred on 02.02.2018 and for argument's sake, if it was vehicle no.7002 with which the accident in question was caused then its driver is not before this Tribunal as a respondent in whose absence without fixing liability on the driver of the vehicle that had caused the accident rashly or negligently, no liability on the owner of such vehicle could be fixed.
79. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the judgment titled as Sithara N.S. & Ors. v. Sai Ram General Insurance Co. Ltd., CIVIL APPEAL Nos.14718-14719 of 2025, dated 12.12.2025, in paragraph 19 has observed, "...liability under the Motor Vehicles Act must be established through credible evidence."
Had filing of the charge-sheet sufficient to prove the rash and negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle in causing the accident 'in each and every case' then, the issue no.1 would not have been drafted as it has been drafted but rather the issue no.1 would have been, 'Whether the charge-sheet by the Investigating Officer in the FIR registered against the driver of the offending vehicle has been filed'.
And if the answer of the issue no.1 would have been affirmative, the Tribunal would have been under no obligation to conduct any further enquiry except quantifying the quantum of compensation and would have allowed each and every claim petition in which the charge-sheet would have been filed.
It would have the effect of making the Tribunal slave to the opinion of the Investigating officer and denuding the power and jurisdiction of the Tribunal under section 165 of the Motor Vehicles Act read with Rule 31 of Annexure XIII of Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.
